_why: Each tool the MCP server registers, with the CLI operation that replaces it, the switch that gates both, and every deliberate difference between them. tests/test_mcp_parity_checklist.py fails when a registered tool has no row or a row names a tool the server does not register. `open` lists what is not decided yet, and must be empty before the MCP server is removed.
every_operation: Reached by the roleband CLI over loopback HTTP to the running engine; the client opens no database. The MCP server opens the database itself and answers with the engine stopped.
One JSON envelope (ok, data, error, meta) with a typed error code and a process exit code, in place of a raised PermissionError, LookupError or ValueError.
meta carries the durable workspace_id; the rotating engine session is reported apart from it.
Unknown input keys and flags are rejected, never ignored.
Gated by the same two switches, read from the database on every call, so a change in Settings applies at once.
Every call acts as the one legacy agent principal, as an MCP call does today.

differences: Also reports workspace_id, engine_session_id, the engine version and the trust mode of the connection.
The transport is loopback HTTP to the engine, not stdio; the command fails as a connection error when no engine runs.

Strict filters: a company, family or location that matches nothing fails with a lookup hint naming the vocabulary command. The MCP tool lists it in `ignored`, drops a filter whose every value was unknown and widens the search.
Case and separators are still normalized, and nothing fuzzier is matched.

The Board's full filter set: level bands, tracks, workplace types, domains, base pay bounds and discloses pay, besides text, companies, families, locations, minimum estimated pay, saved only and the first-seen window.
The Board's sorts, best match included; the MCP tool offers newest, oldest and compensation.
Cursor paging over a deterministic sort with an ID tie-breaker; the MCP tool returns one page.
The default page is sized to the smallest certified context; more fields need --fields or --view.
A first-seen window below one day is an input error; the MCP tool lists it in `ignored`.

The text query takes the Board's search: whole words through the search index, and best match ranks exact, close and related matches. The MCP tool matches the letters anywhere in title, company and description.
A limit outside the declared range is an input error naming the range, as the Board's API refuses one; the MCP tool clamps it to 1 to 100.
Declared views (summary, detail, evidence); the description comes with --view detail.
A description over the view's budget returns a typed excerpt marked truncated, or payload_too_large with a smaller view; the MCP tool returns the full text unbounded.
An unknown ID is a not-found error code, not a raised LookupError.
Cursor paging; the MCP tool returns one page of up to 100.
Each pursuit carries its revision, which a patch passes back.
pursuits.get reads one pursuit with its notes by opportunity ID; the MCP server has no single-pursuit tool.
An idempotency key: the client generates one when none is given and returns it in meta and in a timeout error; a retry with the same key replays the stored result.
receipts.get looks a write up by its key after a lost reply.
The result carries the pursuit's revision.
The audit event records that the write came through the CLI.
Explicit null clears a nullable field (notes, next action, its due date); an omitted field is unchanged. The MCP tool reads null as not given, so it cannot clear a field.
stage: null and priority: null are input errors.
--if-revision N is required: a dashboard edit between the agent's read and its write returns revision_conflict instead of overwriting it.
An idempotency key, replay before the revision check, and receipts.get, as for pursuits.save.
Input arrives as JSON through --input; a patch with no field is refused, as today.
